Rashi on Nazir 42a:10:1.hebrew: להשיר נימין המדולדלים - מן הראש, אבל עדיין לא נעקרו לגמרי. וכיון דמתכוין להשיר כי סורק במסרק, הוה ליה דבר שמתכוין, ואסור:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:10:1.english: To shed loose hairs - [Loosened] from the head, but they have not yet been completely uprooted. And since he intends to shed [them] when he combs with a comb, it is an intentional act, and [is therefore] forbidden.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:13:1.hebrew: אי אמרת מפני המשרת תנן כלל כלל לא - דמשמע: לא יחוף בשום אדמה, גזירה שאינה משרת מפני המשרת:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:13:1.english: If you say we learned "Because of that which removes," not at all - For it implies that he may not shampoo with any earth, [as] a decree [prohibiting earth] that does not remove [hair] on account of [earth] that does remove [hair].

Rashi on Nazir 42a:1:1.english: Behold, “You shall make for yourself fringes” - And it overrides the prohibition of “You shall not wear diverse kinds.”

Rashi on Nazir 42a:2:1.hebrew: אמר רב אחא בריה דרב איקא - מדקתני "או ששיירו שתי שערות לא עשה כלום", זאת אומרת דרובו חשוב ככולו מדאורייתא. דמדכתב הכא "וגילח את ראשו ביום השביעי", ולא מיצטריך ליה למיכתב "ביום השביעי יגלחנו" — לומר דלא חשיב גילוח עד דאיכא כולו שיער מגולח — מכלל מדאיצטריך ליה קרא לאשמועינן דליגלח כולו, דאי לאו האי קרא הוה אמינא דברובו סגי ליה, דרובו ככולו דאורייתא:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:2:1.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said - From [the fact] that it teaches: “Or if they left two hairs [uncut], he has done nothing,” that is to say that the majority [of an entity] is considered like all of it by Torah law. For since it is written here: “And he shall shave his head... on the seventh day,” and it was not necessary for it to write: “On the seventh day he shall shave it,” [except] to say that it is not considered shaving until all the hair is shaved — by implication, since Scripture needed to teach us that he must shave all of it, were it not for this verse, I would have said that [shaving] the majority of it is sufficient for him, as [generally] the majority is like all of it by Torah law.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:4:1.hebrew: האי - "ביום השביעי יגלחנו" בנזיר טמא הוא דכתיב, אבל בנזיר טהור לא כתיב אלא "וגילח את שער ראש נזרו", דלא משמע ליה הכי:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:4:1.english: This - "On the seventh day he shall shave it" is written regarding an impure nazirite; but regarding a pure nazirite, it is only written: "And he shall shave the hair of the head of his naziriteship," which does not imply this to him.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:4:2.hebrew: מחכו עלה במערבא - אהא אתקפתא דר' יוסי בר' חנינא:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:4:2.english: They laughed at it in the West - At this objection of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:4:3.hebrew: דמכדי נזיר טמא דבתער מנלן מנזיר טהור יליף - מדכתיב ביה תער — אי לרבי כדאית ליה, ולת"ק כדאית ליה — וכדלעיל. וה"ה נמי דליתי נזיר טהור מנזיר טמא: מה נזיר טמא כו'. והכא הוא דגלי רחמנא כולו, הא בעלמא רובו ככולו, וכדרב אחא בריה דרב איקא. וא"ת: ליגמר מיניה? הא לא אפשר, משום דהוו להו נזיר ומצורע שני כתובין כאחד:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:4:3.english: After all, from where do we [derive that] an impure nazirite [shaves] with a razor? It is derived from a pure nazirite - Since "a razor" is written with regard to him — whether according to Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] as he holds, or according to the First Tanna as he holds — and as [explained] above. And the same [logic] applies as well, that a pure nazirite should be derived from an impure nazirite: "Just as an impure nazirite, etc." And it is here that the Merciful One revealed [that] all of it [must be shaved], whereas in general the majority of it is like all of it, and in accordance with [the statement of] Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika. And if you should say: Let [other cases] be derived from it? That is not possible, because a nazirite and a leper are two verses [that come] as one [and do not teach other cases].

Rashi on Nazir 42a:5:1.hebrew: וצמח ראשו וחזר וגילחן - נמי לאותן ב' שערות:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:5:1.english: And his head grew [hair] and he again shaved them - [He shaved] those two hairs as well.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:5:2.hebrew: מהו - מי אמרינן: כיון דמעיקרא, כי שייר אותן שתי שערות, לא עשה ולא כלום — השתא נמי, כיון דהדר וצמח, לא עשה ולא כלום, דכמאן דמגלח שתי שערות מעיקרן דמי, ומעכבי? או דלמא, כיון דהשתא קא מיגלח להו, להאי דהדר צמח לא חיישינן, ולא מעכבי:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:5:2.english: What is [the halakha] - Do we say: Since initially, when he left over those two hairs, he accomplished nothing, now too, since [his hair] grew back, he has accomplished nothing, for it is as though he is shaving [just] two hairs from the outset, and they impede [fulfillment]? Or perhaps, since he is now shaving them, we are not concerned with that [hair] which grew back, and they do not impede [it]?

Rashi on Nazir 42a:6:1.hebrew: גילח שערה קמיבעיא ליה לרבא - פשיטא, דכיון דגילח את כל ראשו לבר מהנך ב' שערות, דכי הדר גילח אחת מהן ונשרה חבירתה — שפיר, דקאזיל ומיגלח כי אורחיה, כמאן דאזיל ומגלח שערו; ולההיא דנשרה, מאי הוה ליה למיעבד:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:6:1.english: Is Rava raising a dilemma [as to whether one can] shave [one] hair [at a time]? - It is obvious [that it is valid]: For since he shaved his entire head except for those two hairs, when he went back and shaved one of them and the other one fell out, [it is] fine, as he was proceeding to shave in his usual manner, like one who proceeds and shaves his hair; and as for that [hair] which fell out, what could he have done?

Rashi on Nazir 42a:7:1.hebrew: אלא אימא נשרה אחת וגילח אחת קמבעיא ליה - מי אמרינן: כיון דכל שערו גילח חוץ משער אחת שפיר דמי, דהא לא שייר שתי שערות בלא גילוח? או דלמא, כיון דמעיקרא שייר לו שתי שערות לאו כלום עבד, וכי חזר וגילח אחת לאחר נשירתה דחבירתה נמי לאו כלום עבד, דכיון דלא הוי השתא בראשו אלא שערה אחת לא איקרי גילוח, וכנשרו שניהם דמי — דכי היכי דאם גילח ושייר שערה אחת שפיר גילח, דשערה כנטולה דמי, הכי נמי, כי נשרה אחת, משעת נשירותה הויא חבירתה כנטולה, וכי חזר וגילחה לאו כלום עבד, דכנטולה דמיא:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:7:1.english: Rather, say: One fell out and he shaved one, is what he is asking - Do we say: Since he shaved all his hair except for one hair, it is valid, for he did not leave two hairs without shaving? Or perhaps, since initially he left two hairs, he accomplished nothing, and when he went back and shaved one after the other fell out, he also accomplished nothing — for since there is now only one hair on his head, [shaving it] is not called "shaving," and it is considered as if both of them fell out? For just as if he shaved and left [only] one hair, he shaved properly, because [a single remaining] hair is considered as [already] removed, so too, when one fell out, from the moment it fell out, its counterpart was considered as [already] removed, and when he went back and shaved it, he accomplished nothing, as it was [already] considered as removed.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:7:2.hebrew: א"ל - אי אמרת "גילוח אין כאן", דדמי ליה כמי שיש שיער בכאן:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:7:2.english: [Ravina] said to him - If you say, 'There is no shaving here,' [this implies] that he is considered like one who has hair here.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:7:3.english: [This is what] I said: [Even though] there is no hair here, there is no mitzvah of shaving here - However, after the fact, it is fine.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:8:1.hebrew: נזיר חופף ומפספס - חופף — כמו ״חופף עליו כל היום״ (דברים ל״ג:י״ב) — לשון מגרד. ובלעז: פרי"ר (פריי"ר: לשפשף):
Rashi on Nazir 42a:8:1.english: A nazirite may shampoo and separate - “Ḥofef” — like “He shields him all day” (Deuteronomy 33:12) — is an expression of scratching. And in Old French: freier (to rub).

Rashi on Nazir 42a:8:2.hebrew: מפספס - שמפריד שערותיו זו מזו, אבל לא במסרק:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:8:2.english: Separates - That he separates his hairs from one another, but not with a comb.

Rashi on Nazir 42a:9:1.hebrew: אתאן - לר"י, דאמר: דבר שאין מתכוין — אסור:
Rashi on Nazir 42a:9:1.english: We have come - To Rabbi Yehuda, who says: An unintentional act is forbidden.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:10:1.english: ["Anyone who combs"] to remove loose hairs - Which are not firmly attached and are easy to detach.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:11:1.hebrew: ר"י אומר לא יחוף - כדאמר בגמ':
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:11:1.english: "Rabbi Yishmael says: He may not shampoo" - As [the Gemara] states in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:12:1.hebrew: [מפני שהיא] משרת תנן - לא יחוף אותו באדמה מין שמשרת דוקא, או דלמא ״מפני שמשרת״ — דכל אדמה גזרינן אטו אותה דמשרת:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:12:1.english: [“Because it] removes [hair]” we learned - [Does this mean] he may not shampoo it with earth — specifically a type that removes [hair]? Or perhaps “because of that which removes [hair],” for we decree [against] all earth on account of that [type] which removes [hair]?

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:14:1.hebrew: נזיר שהיה שותה יין כל היום אינו חייב אלא אחת אמרו לו אל תשתה אל תשתה - שהתרו בו על כל פעם ופעם שהוא שותה, חייב על כל אחת ואחת. וכמו כן תגלחת, וכן טומאה, כדמפרש ואזיל:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:14:1.english: "A nazirite who was drinking wine all day is liable [to receive] only one [set of lashes]; [if] they said to him: 'Do not drink, do not drink'" - [This means] that they warned him for each and every time that he drinks, [and therefore] he is liable for each and every one. And likewise [regarding] shaving, and likewise [regarding] ritual impurity, as [the Mishnah] goes on to explain.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:2:1.hebrew: אמר מר וכו' או ששיירו שתי שערות לא עשו ולא כלום וכו' זאת אומרת דרובו ככולו דאורייתא - מדגלי רחמנא גבי נזיר: "ביום השביעי יגלחנו" — דלא איצטריך, דכבר כתיב "וגילח" — אלא לאשמועינן דבעינן תגלחת מצוה שלימה, שלא שיירה כלום:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:2:1.english: The Master said, etc., "or if they left two hairs they have done nothing," etc., "that is to say that the majority of an entity is like all of it by Torah law" - [This is derived] from [the fact] that the Merciful One revealed with regard to a nazirite: “On the seventh day he shall shave it” (Numbers 6:9) — which was unnecessary, as it is already written: “and he shall shave [his head]” (ibid.) — rather, [it comes] to teach us that we require a complete mitzvah shaving, leaving nothing [uncut].

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:3:1.hebrew: הכא הוא דבעי כולו הא בעלמא רובו ככולו - אומר הר"ם: דבעלמא קיימי. מיהו פאת זקן — אמר סוף פרק המצניע (שבת דף צד:) דמלא פי הזוג מיחייב, דמשמע פורתא:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:3:1.english: "It is here that all of it is required, but in general the majority is like all of it" - Rabbeinu Meir says that we are dealing with [shaving] in general. However, [regarding] the corner of the beard, [the Gemara] said at the end of the chapter [entitled] HaMatzni'a (Shabbat 94b) that [for removing] enough to fill the opening of the shears one is liable, which implies a small amount.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:4:1.hebrew: מתקיף לה ר' יוסי בר' חנינא האי בנזיר טמא כתיב - [דכתיב: "ביום השביעי יגלחנו"], דמשמע כולו; וברייתא משתמעא אף בנזיר טהור, שיהא שתי שערות מעכבות:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:4:1.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, objects to this: "This is written with regard to an impure nazirite" - [For it is written: "On the seventh day he shall shave it,"] which implies all of it; whereas the baraita implies even with regard to a pure nazirite that [leaving] two hairs prevents [the shaving from being valid].

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:4:2.hebrew: מחכו עלה במערבא - בפ' קמא דסנהדרין (דף יז:) אמר: "מחכו עלה במערבא" — היינו ר' יוסי בר' חנינא; והכא אשכחן מחכו על דבריו:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:4:2.english: "They laughed at it in the West" - In the first chapter of Sanhedrin (17b), [the Gemara] says [that] "they laughed at it in the West" is Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina; yet here we find [that] they laughed at his words.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:4:3.english: "After all, an impure nazirite [from where do we derive that it is with a razor?] is derived from a pure nazirite (with a razor), so let a pure nazirite come and derive from an impure nazirite" - That [leaving] two hairs invalidates [the shaving].

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:5:1.hebrew: נזיר שגילח ושייר ב' שערות - ובאותה שעה לא גילח יפה, ואח"כ המתין לגלח שתי שערות עד אשר [צמחו שער] ראשו, וחזר וגילחן לאותן שתי שערות לבד — מי אמרינן: אותו תגלחת שתי שערות לא כלום הוא, [הואיל] וכשגילחן ראשו מלא שער:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:5:1.english: “A nazirite who shaved and left two hairs” - And at that time he did not shave properly, and afterward he waited to shave the two hairs until [the hair of] his head grew, and he went back and shaved those two hairs alone — do we say [that] that shaving of two hairs is of no effect, [since] when he shaved them his head was full of hair?

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:6:1.hebrew: נזיר שגילח והניח שתי שערות וגילח אחת ונשרה אחת - כלומר: השניה — מהו? מי אמרינן: כיון דלא גילח שתי שערות לאו גילוח הוא, ששתי שערות אית בהו שיעור גילוח; או דלמא, השתא מיהא לאו איכא שער כלל:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:6:1.english: "A nazirite who shaved and left two hairs, and shaved one and one fell out" - That is to say: [Regarding] the second [hair], what is [the ruling]? Do we say: Since he did not shave two hairs, it is not [considered an act of] shaving, for two hairs constitute the [minimum] measure of shaving; or perhaps, now at any rate there is no hair at all [remaining]?

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:6:2.hebrew: אמר [ליה] רב אחא מדפתי לרבינא גילח שערה מבעיא ליה לרבא - בתמיה. כלומר: הא ודאי גילוח הוי, כיון שבא לגלח הוי שיעור גילוח:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:6:2.english: Rav Aḥa of Difti said [to him], to Ravina: Is Rava raising a dilemma [about one who] shaved a hair? - [This was asked] in astonishment. That is to say: Surely this is certainly [a valid] shaving, since when he came to shave, there was the [requisite] measure of shaving.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:7:1.hebrew: אימא נשרה אחת וגלח אחת - כשבא לגלח שיער, ה"ג רש"י: מי אמרינן השתא מיהא שיער [אין כאן? א"ל:] גילוח אין כאן, שיער אין כאן:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:7:1.english: "Say: One fell out and he shaved one" - When he came to shave hair, this is Rashi's reading: Do we say, "Now, at any rate, there is no hair here"? [He said to him:] "There is no shaving here, there is no hair here."

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:7:2.hebrew: אי שיער אין כאן יש כאן גילוח ה"ק אע"פ ששיער אין כאן מצות גילוח [אין] כאן - הואיל דבתגלחת ראשונה שייר ב' שערות, ובתגלחת זאת לא היה רק שער א':
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:7:2.english: "If there is no hair here, there is shaving here; this is what he said: Even though there is no hair here, the mitzvah of shaving [is not] here" - Since in the first shaving he left two hairs, and in this shaving there was only one hair.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:8:1.hebrew: נזיר חופף ומפספס - פרי"ר בלע"ז — שיחוף ראשו בנתר ובאדמה. אף כי פעמים שמשיר שיער, דבר שאין מתכוין הוא, ומותר לר' שמעון. ומפספס — שמבדיל שערות זו מזו, אף כי פעמים שמשיר:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:8:1.english: "A nazirite may shampoo and separate" - Froier in Old French [meaning to rub] — that he may wash his head with natron and with earth. Even though at times he causes hair to fall out, it is an unintentional act [davar she’eino mitkavein], and [this] is permitted according to Rabbi Shimon. And "separates" — that he separates hairs one from another, even though at times he causes [hair] to fall out.

Tosafot on Nazir 42a:8:2.hebrew: אבל לא סורק - בגמ' משמע דסתם סורק מתכוין להסיר השער:
Tosafot on Nazir 42a:8:2.english: "However, he may not comb" - In the Gemara it implies that ordinarily, one who combs intends to remove the hair.
